SMTO-PRX-0016 — Your Proxmox account isn't allowed to do this

GUID: 7f8dc052-5c3b-42dc-a832-46db862940ff
Slug: proxmox-permission-denied
Domain: PRX · Subsystem: prx

What happened

  • Proxmox recognized the account SMTO signed in with, but that account doesn't have permission for this VM or action. Proxmox refused the request.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Note which VM and action you asked for, and ask the person who manages Proxmox to give your account permission for just that, for example power control on that VM. Proxmox decides access per account and per VM, so this is fixed on the Proxmox side.
  2. If you have a different Proxmox account meant for this work, open Parameter Store, select your Proxmox parameter, open the Value tab, select Reveal & edit value, update "username" and "password", and select Save. SMTO acts with whichever account is saved in that parameter.
  3. Once the permission is in place, send your request again as a new message. The new request signs in again and picks up the account's new permissions.

What success looks like

  • The Agent completes the action on the VM without a permission message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages Proxmox. Ask only for the access this task needs; don't ask for full administrator rights just to get past this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Proxmox returned 403: the authenticated account lacks the privilege required for the requested API path or guest.

What this means

  • The Proxmox response has status 403 after more specific transport/auth mappings do not apply. Proxmox task and resource receipts own effect truth. A failed read, expired local wait or invalid response does not undo a mutation; diagnostics never replay writes or escalate graceful shutdown to forced stop.

Why this can happen

  • The Proxmox response has status 403 after more specific transport/auth mappings do not apply.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact role/resource privilege and endpoint; do not infer that logging in again will grant permission.

How to fix it

  • Identify the API path in Technical details and grant the account (or its group or API token role) only the required privilege on that path in PVE under Datacenter › Permissions, for example VM.PowerMgmt for power actions or VM.Audit for status reads. Do not grant broad Administrator roles; alternatively save a different, correctly scoped account in the Proxmox Server parameter.
  • Use an account with the intended Proxmox role and resource privilege, or explicitly repair that role assignment.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended authorized account has the required resource privilege.

What not to do

  • Do not grant broad permissions; verify the exact resource, identity and required access.

Technical notes

  • Proxmox task and resource receipts own effect truth. A failed read, expired local wait or invalid response does not undo a mutation; diagnostics never replay writes or escalate graceful shutdown to forced stop.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
